A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Localized Point Management (LPM) research despite the changed title and formatting. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original LPM experiments on static and dynamic scenes, including benchmark results, component ablations, sparse-view experiments and per-scene appendix results.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains these original experiments and reports additional Gaussian-model comparisons, cost measurements and qualitative geometry results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same error maps, LightGlue correspondence matching, intersecting-cone zone identification, local densification, sparse-zone point insertion, opacity reset and density-aware pruning. Applications to additional Gaussian models do not establish a changed LPM procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 13 static scenes from Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending, plus six Neural 3D Video scenes and the same sparse-view scenarios. The stated total changes from 11 to 13, correcting v1's inconsistent count rather than adding scenes. New geometry visualizations analyze the retained reconstruction coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds 2DGS, MipGS and PixelGS, each evaluated with and without LPM. The cost comparison expands from standard/lower-threshold 3DGS and LPM in v1 Table 3 to include GaussianPro and PixelGS in v3 Table 4. GaussianPro reports results on Truck and an out-of-memory outcome on PlayRoom. Existing dynamic comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: Dynamic-results Table 2 removes DSSIM1 and retains the former DSSIM2 values under the single heading DSSIM, reducing reported metric coverage. Additional host-model configurations are evaluated, while the original train/test splits, 30,000-iteration budget and half-resolution dynamic evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cost-effectiveness analysis gains comparisons against competing densification methods, and Figure 3 adds a depth example and a 2DGS mesh comparison. The original component ablations, lower-threshold experiment and sparse-view study are retained; the sparse-view study moves to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Retrained-model markers do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands concrete results through additional Table 1 model comparisons, cost outcomes, qualitative geometry findings and the new indoor/outdoor 2DGS Table 12. For example, Table 1 newly reports Mip-NeRF 360 PSNR of 27.54 for PixelGS and 27.80 with LPM. Existing 3DGS/STGS benchmark and per-scene scores remain unchanged; DSSIM1 result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The Gaussian representation, covariance parameterization, alpha-blending expression and correspondence/projection mathematics are unchanged. Added explanations of correspondence indices and region symbols clarify existing notation rather than introduce mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The core claims about localized correction of ADC failures and applicability to static and dynamic Gaussian models remain. v3 makes minimal additional training cost an explicit abstract-level claim and introduces a concrete efficiency contrast with GaussianPro and PixelGS in the introduction.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds explanations attributing efficiency to fast feature matching, pruning that limits model growth and parallel matrix operations. The results discussion interprets new depth/mesh comparisons as evidence of geometry calibration. The limitation that inherited 3DGS densification rules may be suboptimal remains in the conclusion.

D1.justification: v3 Table 4 explicitly states that LPM training time includes feature matching, and the text newly identifies parallel matrix operations. The project-page address also changes. The RTX 3090, 24 GB memory, 30,000 iterations and offline matching were already documented in v1; these are not new settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for 2DGS, PatchMatch and Photo Tourism and sharpens its efficiency positioning against GaussianPro and PixelGS. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged. Bibliography entries for several still-tabulated dynamic baselines, including HyperReel and StreamRF, disappear without removing those methods from the comparisons.

P1.justification: The title changes, several abstract/introduction/results passages are revised, notation receives local clarification, and equal-contribution markings change. The sparse-view discussion moves to the reorganized supplement. Most methodological exposition and the overall introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion structure remain.

P2.justification: The paper switches from single-column to two-column presentation and moves Figure 1 onto the opening page. Figure 2 gains explanatory labels, Figure 3 gains depth/mesh panels, and displaced RGB examples join Figure 6 in the supplement. Tables are expanded and restyled, the dynamic table loses a metric column, and a new indoor/outdoor table is added.

improvement.justification: The additional model evaluations and direct GaussianPro/PixelGS cost comparisons strengthen evidence for LPM's compatibility and efficiency while retaining the original experiments and ablations. Geometry visualizations and clearer diagram labels also help. These gains are tempered by removed DSSIM1 results and weak documentation of new Table 12, whose caption refers to 3DGS despite showing 2DGS rows. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
